newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Lindsey says U.S. economy well-balanced.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Lindsey says U.S. economy well-balanced.

text.p: Outgoing Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey on Tuesday described the economy as well-balanced and said it remained on a path of moderate growth.
"I think we have a very well-balanced economy," Lindsey said in an interview with the Cavuto Business Report on the Fox television network.
"We are in a period of contained inflation," he added.
Lindsey said that wage rises in the fourth quarter were running at a 4.8 percent annual rate but attributed 20 percent of that to the recent increase in the minimum wage.
Excluding the impact of the minimum wage, he said that wage growth was running at about four percent.

"There may be a little bit of a wage pickup but it's not necessarily an inflationary thing," Lindsey said. He stressed that the wage pickup comes after very small increases in wages over the past four or five years.

Asked whether wage inflation was beginning to develop in the economy, the Fed official replied, "We are certainly seeing the beginning of wage inflation but whether or not this passes into prices we don't know."

Finally, Lindsey was questioned about what the Fed focuses on when making decisions about interest rates. He pointed out that there are 19 policymakers involved in the Federal Open Market Committee deliberations with each individual offering a different perspective.
The result is the Fed takes "almost everything into account," he said.
Lindsey is planning to leave the Fed at the beginning of next month to return to the private sector. He plans to take up a position at the American Enterprise Institute think tank.
